title: morella salicifolia subsp. kilimandscharica
intro: Morella salicifolia subsp. kilimandscharica, commonly known as the East African willow, is a subspecies of flowering plant in the family Myricaceae. It is a shrub or small tree native to East Africa, valued for its medicinal properties and traditional uses. The East African willow has been traditionally used to treat various health issues, including fever, rheumatism, and digestive problems, due to its health benefits such as anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties. Its therapeutic actions include reducing inflammation, relieving pain, and protecting against oxidative stress, primarily attributed to the presence of bioactive constituents like flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids.
